key_insight: A Monte Carlo framework can convert published aggregate trial results into patient-level risk estimates for rare cancers, using Ewing sarcoma as a proof of concept.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help refine survivorship surveillance and future trial design, but it is not yet a substitute for patient-level validated decision support.
method: Integrates genetic risk, serial biomarkers, ctDNA-MRD, and competing mortality
Adds long-term toxicity modules across five organ systems
evidence_signal: In Ewing sarcoma data from more than 3,400 patients, the model reported 3.2% mean absolute error across 23 efficacy endpoints and stayed within published confidence intervals for all 20 toxicity endpoints.
watch_item: The framework is validated on published aggregate data, so transfer to other rare cancers and real-world patient-level use still requires future validation.
paper_title: WITHDRAWN: Multi-Timepoint Risk Stratification in Rare Cancers: A Computational Framework Validated against Published Ewing Sarcoma Trial Data
